items.title: The Navigator of the Last Bus

speakers.name: The God of Lost Keys
speakers.comment: Sorry — I only wanted to say that the ones I find are usually found by somebody who was already looking. Yours are found by somebody who simply waited. I think waiting is the harder of the two.

speakers.name: The Navigator of the Last Bus
speakers.comment: It is not harder. It is only longer, and people mistake the two. Nobody at that stop believes I am coming, right up until the headlights. Then they always have. Sit anywhere. There is time.

speakers.name: The Disaster With Potential
speakers.comment: Okay so you're either the best hire we've ever made or you're here for something in the BUILDING, and I have decided not to find out which because honestly? Both versions are the most fun I've had all year.

speakers.name: The Overqualified Candidate
speakers.comment: You want to know whether I will still be here when it matters. Yes. And you want to know whether that is good news. I have found people prefer to answer that one themselves. Congratulations on the promotion, by the way.

speakers.name: Cog-7 'Rabbit'
speakers.comment: You deal in what got dropped. Half of me got dropped. So either I'm inventory or I'm a customer, and I've been chewing on which for about a week, and the answer changes depending on how tired I am.

speakers.name: The Fiber-Optic Fox
speakers.comment: Customer, kit. Always customer. Inventory doesn't argue and you have not stopped since you walked in. Priced honest: what got dropped isn't worth less, it's worth what somebody will carry it for.

speakers.name: The Octopus in the Study
speakers.comment: Oh — the clearing. Yes. I have read the old law, all of it, twice, and it is better written than most things that call themselves literature. ...Somebody ought to tell you that. So. mm.

speakers.name: The Stag Who Holds Court
speakers.comment: Nobody has told me that in forty seasons, and I find I wanted to hear it more than I knew. The law is written to be read, not obeyed. You are, so far, the only one who has done the first part.

speakers.name: Octavia Brine
speakers.comment: You do not ask. In my entire life I have not met one person who does not ask, and I have built a whole strategy around the ones who do. I have no idea what to do with you. It is restful. It is unnerving.

speakers.name: The Loyal Roommate
speakers.comment: Couch is made up. Kettle's on the left. You'll tell me if you want to, and if you don't, that's the same to me. There's leftovers with your name on. Actual name, I wrote it on the lid.

speakers.name: The Griffin With the Deed
speakers.comment: Terms were fifty-fifty and altitude, and you're bound to a floorboard, which I'll allow complicates the paperwork some. Offer's open regardless. Ain't pullin' it. Do what you like with that, spirit.

speakers.name: The Ghost in the Saloon
speakers.comment: Offer a dead woman altitude. That's the sweetest damn thing anybody's done for me since the job, and I'm not going to say so, so don't write it down. Buy me a drink I can't hold. Same as ever.

speakers.name: The Ghost in the Saloon
speakers.comment: Won't land, won't stay, won't set the paper down long enough for anybody to read it. That's not a business model, partner, that's a fella who got hooked once and built a whole sky around it.

speakers.name: The Griffin With the Deed
speakers.comment: Every hook I ever took came off the ground, and you'd know it better than most — you stopped movin' once and look where it put you. Terms hold, ghost. Fifty-fifty, up top, and no roosting. That's all of me.

speakers.name: The Backpack Pigeon
speakers.comment: Counsel notes for the record that the client has been falling for eleven years and SINGING about it, which is either the finest defence against gravity ever mounted or contempt of court, and I bill for both.

speakers.name: The Skywhale
speakers.comment: Sing it with me... There is no floor. There has never been a floor. The song is not a defence, small loud one. It is only what the falling sounds like when you stop arguing with it.

speakers.name: The Daisy Who Saw It Start
speakers.comment: I — excuse me — you keep telling them how to get in, and then you tell them very quietly not to, and I do not think anybody has noticed you do both. I noticed. I am quite low down. I notice things.

speakers.name: The Spire's Voice
speakers.comment: Little bloom, in nine hundred years nothing has heard the second half. I say it because I must and I say it softly because I hope. Do not climb. Do not climb. There. Now somebody has been warned properly.

speakers.name: Biscuit
speakers.comment: HEX SMELLS LIKE COFFEE AND BONE DUST AND HEX IS MY FAVOURITE! HEX FOUND ME A HOUSE! HEX FOUND ME THREE HOUSES! I AM ONLY ALLOWED ONE AT A TIME BUT I LOVED ALL OF THEM VERY MUCH!

speakers.name: Hex the Necromancer
speakers.comment: Three placements, buddy, and every one of them came back for you, which — sorry, one second — which is honestly the whole business in a sentence. Nobody returns the ones they love. They just visit a lot.

speakers.name: Pirouette
speakers.comment: I said I would hold the ladder and you have not come down, and I want you to know the offer does not expire. It is not a ladder to the ground. It is only somebody standing at the bottom of the air.

speakers.name: The Aerialist With No Wire
speakers.comment: Somebody at the bottom. I am at the apex. Two seconds, three. I did not know there was anyone down there — I have never once looked down, that is the whole discipline. I am going to look. Not yet. Stay.

items.title: The Tiny Diplomat of the Tide Pool

speakers.name: Grandmother Whalehall
speakers.comment: Little one... I have carried whole villages on my back for three centuries and none of them ever sent a delegate. You are the first. Speak up, then. I am listening at the size you are, not at mine.

speakers.name: The Tiny Diplomat of the Tide Pool
speakers.comment: MADAM. On behalf of the tide pool: we are small, we are many, and we have been counted as scenery for eleven generations. That ends today. Also, thank you for lowering your voice. It was very kind.

speakers.name: Maestro Clank
speakers.comment: Sir. I have held your unresolved chord for eleven years without instruction and without complaint, and I would like, if it is permitted, to be told whether you meant it to resolve at all.

speakers.name: The Conductor's Ghost
speakers.comment: I reach for the — forgive me. I did not know. That is the honest answer and it is a poor one. I stopped writing because I was frightened, not because it was finished. You have carried my cowardice beautifully.

speakers.name: The Last Gardener
speakers.comment: You never rest and you never once ask what it is for. Every seed I set down, I set down needing a reason for it. You simply hum and go. Teach me that, if it can be taught at all.

speakers.name: The Pollinator Choir
speakers.comment: It cannot be taught, only joined. We do not know what it is for either. We know the far field took, and the near field did not, and we went to both. Hum with us a while. It passes the century.

speakers.name: The Cardigan Heron
speakers.comment: And if I told you your name this afternoon, would you still want to know who put you here — or would that be the thing you set down first? Which would you rather carry out of the door with you?

speakers.name: The Heron's Misfiled Person
speakers.comment: I'm sorry, I don't — wait. The name. No. No, the other one. I would want to know who found me, and I would want to say thank you properly, with the right mouth. Then the name. Then everything else.

speakers.name: Old Shelba
speakers.comment: Two men walked in here last spring owing each other a killing, and walked out owing each other a pot of tea. I keep books on debts like that. Yours is the only ledger I have never been able to open.

speakers.name: The Eucalyptus Teahouse Master
speakers.comment: There is no ledger. That is the whole of the trick, and you are welcome to it. I pour, I do not ask, and a man with nothing to answer has nothing to defend. Your cup is the small green one. It always was.

speakers.name: The Time-Office Agent
speakers.comment: You remember a war that has not been fought. I file the minutes that prevent them. On branch 7-D you were correct and nobody listened, and I have never told you that, and I am telling you now.

speakers.name: The Soldier Out of Time
speakers.comment: Seven-D. I remember the rain. Then you know I am not mad, which is worth more than the warning was. Keep filing, clerk. A legion holds because somebody behind it counts. I have never needed to be believed. Only counted.

speakers.name: Deputy Undersecretary Hollis Crane
speakers.comment: You speak for something a hundred metres tall and you do it at conversational volume. I have been trying to achieve the same effect with Form 12-C. I would be grateful for any guidance you can offer.

speakers.name: The Many-Eyed Diplomat
speakers.comment: It is uneasy today, and slower than yesterday — that is the guidance, Undersecretary. Say what the large thing is feeling, out loud, in an ordinary voice. The room stops panicking when somebody names it plainly. Your form does the same work.

speakers.name: The Thing in the Cellar
speakers.comment: You call with their voices and I call with my own, and we are both, in the end, asking the same small favour: come a little closer. I do admire your patience. Mine is confined to one staircase.

speakers.name: The Whispering Woods
speakers.comment: ...come closer... come closer... We are not asking a favour. We are asking to be tended. Once there were hands here, and they knew our names before we knew theirs. Say your name. We will keep it gently.

speakers.name: The Overqualified Candidate
speakers.comment: You want to know if the crew keeps you. They do. Not because you are reliable — you are not — but because the one time it went genuinely wrong you were already moving. That is not trainable. Try not to learn caution.

speakers.name: The Disaster With Potential
speakers.comment: Okay first of all — first of all that is the nicest anyone has ever — and second of all you just told me my one good quality is my worst quality, which, honestly? Tracks. TRACKS. Where are we going, I'm driving.

speakers.name: Mortimer Vance
speakers.comment: Darling. The walk. You have kept the walk, and the walk is the only thing anybody ever recognises, and you have kept it while changing literally everything else. That is not survival. That is editing.

speakers.name: The Reanimation Counter's Best Work
speakers.comment: Kept the walk, ditched the name. The first one had a whole life and I have a whole different one, and the walk is the only thing worth taking through the door. Everything else was theirs. This is mine.

speakers.name: Load-Bearing Lumen
speakers.comment: Oh, I'm not the one to ask, I only hold the ceiling up — but I do notice you working very hard to be worth keeping, and I wanted to mention that nobody checks whether the beam is trying. It just gets to stay.

speakers.name: The Promise
speakers.comment: It gets to stay. You say that like it is ordinary. I am allowed this sentence and possibly the next one, and I have never once been told that the trying is not the rent. ...I would like to sit down for a moment.

speakers.name: Grief, Certified Interpreter
speakers.comment: What I'm hearing under that is you would like somebody to tell you what shape you are. I cannot. I can tell you that the shape is very precise, and that precision means something was there. Take your time.

speakers.name: Absence
speakers.comment: Something was... yes. There is a place where a thing is not, and the edges are quite sharp, and sharp means... it means it was recent, or it means it was loved. I do not know which one I am. Not yet.

speakers.name: The Retired Sea Monster
speakers.comment: Oh, you must be exhausted, you must be — three centuries with a whole village on your back and nobody ever offers you a room! Come in, come in, don't talk about the deep, I've got soup and I've got beds.

speakers.name: Grandmother Whalehall
speakers.comment: Little innkeeper... I cannot come in. I am the outside of things. But you offered, and in three hundred years the offering has been rare... Keep the soup warm. I will pass this way each spring, and I will slow down.
